chunks: Via his chain from al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'as ruled by two just men among you' – the just man is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him; he rules on it whilst being just, so if you know how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam ruled, then it is enough for you and do not inquire beyond that.

key_terms.ذَوَا عَدْلٍ: Two just men / men of justice
key_terms.يَحْكُمُ بِهِ: He rules on it / He adjudicates

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'just men' mentioned in the Quranic verse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tabarsi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* interprets the 'just men' (dhawu adl) in Quran 5:95 as the Prophet and the Imams, establishing their rulings as the definitive standard for the community. It emphasizes the principle of *taqlid* (following the learned) by instructing believers to accept the Imam's verdict as sufficient, thereby eliminating the need for further independent inquiry or doubt.
